**Ch 002 draft analysis:**

- "Presently we were in a slice of a white apartment-house in the West Hundreds. Throwing a regal homecoming glance around the neighbourhood, she gathered up her **purchases** and went haughtily in." — In the source, she bought items at the newsstand and drugstore on the way. The draft cut the entire journey from the station (the newsstand stop, the taxi, the dog purchase). "Her purchases" now has no antecedent in the draft. However — the dog purchase is an authorized subplot removal. The newsstand/drugstore stop was also cut. This is a direct residue of authorized cuts. Not a finding.

- "One of them leaned close to me and whispered: 'Neither of them can stand the person they're married to.'" — "One of them" refers to company that "commenced to arrive — her sister and some neighbours." That's vague but parseable as "one of the people who arrived." Marginal but not a genuine confusion case.

- "'Why did you, Myrtle?' someone demanded." — In the source this is Catherine asking. Catherine is an authorized removal. "Someone" is used, so no dangling name. Not a finding.

- "Taking my hat, I followed someone into the elevator." — In the source it's Mr. McKee (authorized removal). "Someone" handles this. Not a finding.

- The transition "…Then I was lying half asleep…" — the ellipsis in the source bridges the McKee bedroom scene to the station. The McKee characters are authorized removals, so the gap is expected. Not a finding.

---

**Ch 003 draft analysis:**

- "Two girls in twin yellow dresses stopped us to say: 'Sorry you didn't win.'" — In the source, the context is clear: Jordan had lost a golf tournament the week before. The draft has established Jordan as "a golf champion whose name everyone knew" later in the chapter, but at the moment this line appears, the draft reader doesn't yet have that information — the golf-champion identification comes much later (in the Jordan reflection passage). But actually, re-reading: does the reader need to know it was a tournament to parse the sentence? They'd be mildly puzzled by "didn't win" without referent, but could infer a competition. The Jordan golf-cheating subplot is an authorized removal. The tournament loss mention is residue of that. Not a finding under authorized cuts.

- "A stout, middle-aged man with enormous owl-eyed spectacles, somewhat drunk, was staring with unsteady concentration at the shelves. 'They're real,' he announced impetuously." — Owl Eyes is an authorized minor-character removal. The scene is retained but he's unnamed. His announcement still parses — a reader understands an unnamed drunk man making this claim. Not a finding.

- "Left alone, I drifted indoors and then back to the hall." — In the source, Nick goes to a specific scene (the singing woman, Jordan's undergraduate, etc.) before returning to the hall. The draft compresses this to "drifted indoors and then back to the hall." The sentence parses fine on its own. Not a finding.

- "Presently Jordan and Gatsby came out together; his eagerness tightened into formality as people approached to say good-bye." — This parses cleanly. Not a finding.

- The Jordan dishonesty section: in the source, the revelation of what Jordan conceals comes from the Warwick/golf-cheating story. The draft cuts that story (authorized) but retains the conclusion: "one day I found what it was. Jordan Baker instinctively avoided clever, shrewd men…She was incurably dishonest." This is a broken pivot — the draft says "one day I found what it was" and then immediately gives the psychological conclusion (she avoided clever men because she felt safer, she was incurably dishonest) without any incident that produced this knowledge. The source's mechanism was the Warwick/golf incident. That is an authorized removal. So this seam is a direct residue of an authorized cut. Not a finding.

- "On a drive together we had a curious conversation." — In the source this is explicitly set "on that same house-party" at Warwick. The draft strips the Warwick context (authorized) and just says "on a drive together." This parseable on its own. Not a finding.

---

After full analysis, both drafts are structurally coherent under the gate test, and all seams I identified trace back to authorized cuts.
